EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The United States has declared an "Economic D-Day" against Iran, implementing unprecedented sanctions and threatening severe secondary consequences for any nation or entity providing a lifeline to Tehran. This aggressive economic posture coincides with heightened military tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, where the US military has established a "secret" shipping corridor, and escalating friction between Israel and Turkey following an Israeli airstrike on a Syrian airbase.

IRAN
The US, led by President Donald Trump, has declared an "Economic D-Day" against Iran, marking the "most crushing economic operation" in history. Trump stated that any country providing a financial lifeline to Iran (e.g., through oil smuggling, currency swaps, cash transfers, shell companies) will face severe economic consequences, asserting that Iran's military capabilities are crippled and its currency worthless. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed these threats as a diversion from America's domestic economic crises (unprecedented debt and soaring interest rates) and warned that continued "failed policies" would only lead to further defeat and Iranian animosity. Trump also reiterated that Iran will "never have a nuclear weapon."

US officials claim that a two-week operation by CENTCOM degraded Iran's radar and maritime surveillance systems in the Strait of Hormuz, limiting Iranian monitoring to a few restored radars and IRGC fast boats. As a result, the US has established a "secret" shipping corridor through the southern channel, facilitating the passage of 15-20 tankers nightly, injecting approximately 10 million barrels of oil daily into global markets (half the pre-war volume). US aircraft provide defense against Iranian cruise missiles and drones; eight Iranian drones and two cruise missiles were reportedly intercepted earlier this week. Trump claims the US has "complete control" of Hormuz and that the maritime blockade has been 100% successful. In contradiction, a source close to the Iranian negotiation team stated no direct talks with the US ever occurred, only via Oman for Hormuz control, and reported the diversion of an Emirati oil tanker in the northern corridor towards Bandar Abbas.

Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf visited Iraq, where he discussed regional developments and bilateral relations with Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi and Chief Justice Faiq Zidan. Qalibaf asserted that the US seeks to plunder regional resources and is behind regional insecurity. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi held phone conversations with the Foreign Minister of Mauritania, emphasizing cooperation among Islamic countries to support Palestine, and with Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir to discuss de-escalation efforts. Iran also demanded compensation from Ukraine for a July 25 "terrorist" attack on an Iranian merchant ship in the Caspian Sea. Senior IRGC Quds Force chief Brigadier General Esmaeil Qa’ani stated that Israel is afflicted with "social cancer" and its internal collapse is "inevitable." Reports suggest Iran is considering striking US military targets in southeastern Europe (e.g., Bulgaria, NATO base in Cyprus) if the US escalates the war.

ISRAEL
Israel conducted an airstrike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria, which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu justified by stating Israel "will not tolerate a Turkish military presence establishing itself further south" that threatens Israeli security. He added, "We conveyed that. Now, we saw that Turkey intends to establish itself at an airport south of its line, near Aleppo, and we conveyed a message. The message was conveyed, but apparently it was not heard, so we made sure they understood it better." IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured the Israeli-held buffer zone in southern Syria and reinforced this stance, stating, "We will not allow hostile forces to establish themselves along our borders."

In the Gaza Strip, the IDF carried out multiple strikes. In the Shati area, four Nukhba Force commanders from Hamas's Beit Lahia Battalion were killed: Muhammad Hamdi Ahmed al-Masri (company commander), Samad Samir Harb Abu Jabal (platoon commander who invaded Israel on October 7, 2023), Muhammad Attar (platoon commander), and Muhammad Fathi Hussein Nasser (platoon commander). The IDF stated these operatives posed a threat to troops. Separately, in central Gaza's Nuseirat, a Hamas company commander who participated in the October 7 onslaught was targeted. Less than 30 minutes later, the IDF and Shin Bet struck a civilian police station in Gaza City, claiming at least four Hamas military wing terrorists and one Popular Resistance Committees terrorist were present, planning attacks on IDF troops. Palestinian media reported six to nine fatalities and 15 wounded in the Gaza City police station strike, and one killed in Nuseirat.

The IDF closed its probe into the killing of seven World Central Kitchen (WCK) aid workers in Gaza in 2024. Australia summoned Israel's ambassador, expressing outrage and stating the decision was "far from the level of accountability we expect." The UK also issued a "rare threat" to Israel, summoning its ambassador over plans for new housing units in E1, calling it an "unacceptable and destructive process," and pledging a response in the coming weeks. The IDF admitted its forces fired on the vehicle carrying five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in Gaza in January 2024 and opened a criminal investigation.

Domestically, a poll showed Eisenkot's party rising to 26 mandates, Likud to 23, and Bennett to 13, while Gantz, Trooper-Handel, and Erdan were below the electoral threshold. The Joint Arab List parties (Hadash, Taal, Balad) officially announced a joint run for the Knesset. Former PM Naftali Bennett presented a new security doctrine, advocating for striking Iran in response to Hezbollah attacks, declaring Qatar an "enemy state," replacing Turkey and Qatar with Egypt in Gaza, and using the IDF/Shin Bet to combat illegal weapons in Israel. A military exercise is scheduled for tomorrow morning in Nahariya.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces conducted multiple strikes in the Gaza Strip. In Shati, four Hamas Nukhba Force commanders, including one who participated in the October 7, 2023 onslaught, were killed. In Nuseirat, a Hamas company commander involved in the October 7 onslaught was targeted. In Gaza City, a police station used by Hamas and Popular Resistance Committees operatives for planning attacks on IDF troops was struck, resulting in at least 9 reported fatalities and 15 wounded, according to Palestinian media. Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya strongly condemned these strikes, calling Israel's actions a mockery of the ceasefire and urging international mediators to intervene immediately to prevent the agreement's collapse.

The IDF confirmed closing its investigation into the killing of seven World Central Kitchen (WCK) aid workers in Gaza in 2024. The inquiry into the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab, who died in January 2024, is ongoing, with the IDF now admitting its forces fired on the vehicle she was in.

In the West Bank, Palestinian reports indicate that settlers set fire to a house in the village of Beit Amra / Khirbat al-Fakhit, south of Hebron. No arrests were made at the time of reporting. A resident of Beitar Illit will be indicted for multiple acts of violence against Israelis and Palestinians, including ramming sheep and trespassing. Firefighting efforts continue for a blaze in the southern Hebron hills, which led to the evacuation of the settlement of Afeka and the closure of Route 60.

LEBANON
The Israeli Air Force conducted strikes in southern Lebanon. Lebanese reports confirm Israeli Air Force attacks in the Ali Taher Ridge area during the night. Additional reports specify an "all-out fire siege" by Israeli forces around Ali Taher Ridge, aimed at cutting off supply lines and isolating Hezbollah operatives in an underground facility. Another Israeli strike reportedly targeted Mansouri in southern Lebanon, where a public water reservoir was allegedly blown up, cutting off water supply.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Israel carried out a strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria. Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani, in an exclusive interview with Israel's Channel 12, stated that Israel had "no legitimate justification for the attack" and denied any intention of establishing a Turkish base at Abu al-Duhur airport. He accused Israel of reneging on commitments made before a US-brokered agreement. Reuters reported that Mossad Chief Roman Gofman spoke with Syrian Foreign Minister al-Shaibani on August 14 regarding Turkey's military presence in Syria, days before the Israeli strike.

Turkish officials, speaking to Middle East Eye, claimed a technical team was at the base two days prior for repairs but no military forces were present, denying Turkey's intent to "take over any base in Syria." They accused Israel of not using the "hotline" with Ankara and "playing with fire." US Ambassador to Turkey and special envoy to Syria, Tom Burke, stated that the Israeli strike "posed a real risk of rapid escalation into direct military confrontation between Israel and Turkey," with Turkish forces almost scrambling fighter jets. Turkey's Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar expressed readiness for Ankara to cooperate with Damascus in oil and gas exploration in Syria.

In Iraq, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf met with Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi, who praised Iran's "firm support" during counter-terrorism efforts, especially against ISIS, and acknowledged the sacrifices of martyrs like Qassem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. Qalibaf stated that foreign powers' intervention in regional equations is rapidly declining, and America is seeking an honorable exit from the region. Head of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Units (PMU), Faleh al-Fayyadh, stated that Iran withstood a "quasi-global war" and maintained cohesion. He noted PMU suffered over 100 martyrs and dozens wounded from aggression against Iraq and that 100 PMU headquarters were bombed during the war on Iran. PMU leadership reiterated commitment to government directives and national security, denying pressures to disband or integrate, and plans to develop capabilities. Iraqi PM called for Iraq to have "special treatment" regarding oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz.

GULF STATES
The United Arab Emirates has declared an immediate halt to all trade with Iran, effective today, in response to missile attacks launched from Iran against the Emirates. The trade volume between the two countries stood at approximately $28 billion in 2024.

The US military has established a "secret" shipping corridor through the southern channel of the Strait of Hormuz, along the coast of Oman. This operation, active for several weeks, sees 15-20 tankers transiting nightly, delivering about 10 million barrels of oil per day to global markets. This has been facilitated by US strikes that degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance capabilities, and US air assets provide protection against Iranian drones and cruise missiles. President Trump asserted that the US has "complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz. However, a source close to the Iranian negotiation team stated that discussions on Hormuz control were held with Oman, not the US, and that talks with the American side were halted after the US violated the Islamabad agreement. The US Treasury is reportedly concerned that Oman might help Iran secure a more favorable nuclear deal.

Houthi forces in Yemen have escalated their maritime operations against Saudi Arabia, declaring a "maritime embargo." Since July 20, they claim to have targeted eight Saudi oil tankers (five in the Red Sea, three in the Gulf of Aden/Arabian Sea) and prevented 48 other Saudi oil tankers from crossing (34 in Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean, 14 in Red Sea). These actions are framed as imposing "three new equations" on Saudi Arabia: "blockade for blockade," striking Saudi mobilizations anywhere, and protecting Yemen's sovereignty. They warn Saudi Arabia of "comprehensive escalation" if aggression continues and demand an end to the blockade, payment of salaries, and withdrawal of occupiers.

Iran's Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, warned southern Persian Gulf states against providing "any assistance" to the US military, stating, "nothing remains hidden from our eyes."

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Declares "Economic D-Day" on Iran**: President Trump announced unprecedented economic sanctions against Iran and threatened severe penalties for any country or entity providing financial support.
2.  **US Establishes "Secret" Hormuz Corridor**: The US military has created a secure shipping lane in the southern Strait of Hormuz, facilitating the nightly passage of 15-20 tankers, moving approximately 10 million barrels of oil daily.
3.  **Israel Strikes Syrian Airbase, Tensions with Turkey Escalate**: Israel attacked Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria, citing Turkish plans for military deployment. Netanyahu issued a strong warning to Turkey, which denied military presence and accused Israel of "playing with fire," while a US envoy highlighted a "real risk of direct military confrontation."
4.  **IDF Kills Hamas Commanders in Gaza**: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed four Nukhba Force commanders from Hamas's Beit Lahia Battalion (including an October 7 participant) in Shati, and targeted multiple operatives at a police station in Gaza City, resulting in up to 9 reported fatalities.
5.  **UAE Halts All Trade with Iran**: The UAE ceased all trade with Iran, a decision that impacts an annual trade volume of $28 billion, following alleged missile attacks from Iran.
6.  **Houthi Maritime Escalation Against Saudi Arabia**: Houthi forces claimed to have targeted 8 Saudi oil tankers and prevented 48 others from crossing various maritime choke points since July 20, imposing a "maritime embargo."
7.  **International Condemnation of Israeli Actions**: The UK summoned Israel's ambassador over E1 settlement plans, threatening sanctions, and Australia summoned Israel's ambassador expressing outrage over the closure of the WCK aid workers' killing probe.
8.  **Mossad Chief-Syrian FM Contact**: Mossad Chief Roman Gofman reportedly spoke with Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani on August 14 regarding Turkish military presence in Syria, days before the Israeli strike.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high across multiple fronts. The "Economic D-Day" declared by the US against Iran signals an intensified economic war, with potential for broader secondary sanctions impacting global trade partners. Military confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz remains an active flashpoint; the US's establishment of a "secret" shipping corridor, combined with Iranian warnings against Gulf states assisting the US and alleged tanker diversions, increases the likelihood of miscalculation or direct engagement. The Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and subsequent warnings to Turkey have significantly raised the risk of a direct military confrontation between Israel and Turkey, with a US envoy acknowledging this almost occurred. Ongoing Israeli military operations in Gaza, targeting Hamas commanders and infrastructure, despite a ceasefire, are highly volatile and could lead to a collapse of the current agreement and renewed widespread conflict, as warned by Hamas. Houthi escalation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden against Saudi oil tankers poses a continuous threat to regional maritime security and energy supply. Iran's consideration of striking US military targets in southeastern Europe (Bulgaria, Cyprus) suggests a potential geographical expansion of conflict if tensions with the US escalate further.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has announced an "Economic D-Day" against Iran, imposing unprecedented sanctions and threatening severe secondary economic consequences for any country aiding Iran. It also established a "secret" shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump has also indicated that the US and Canada have reached a trade agreement and will hold talks. The US national debt has surpassed $40 trillion.
**Iran's** Foreign Minister Araghchi condemned US economic "terrorism" as a global threat. Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf visited Iraq, emphasizing cooperation and regional stability. Iran also demanded compensation from Ukraine for a merchant ship attack and its Foreign Minister held calls with Mauritania and Pakistan.
**Israel's** actions in Syria, Lebanon, and Gaza have drawn international attention.
The **United Kingdom** summoned Israel's ambassador to express opposition to new housing units in E1 (West Bank), deeming it "unacceptable and destructive," and threatened a response in the coming weeks.
**Australia** summoned Israel's ambassador and expressed outrage over the IDF's decision to close the investigation into the killing of World Central Kitchen aid workers, demanding justice.
**France** condemned US sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). France also expelled an Iranian cultural attaché and another diplomat in a reciprocal move after Iran expelled two French cultural attachés.
**Egypt's** Foreign Minister indicated ongoing contacts with Iran related to de-escalation efforts.
**China** urged the US to abandon its "hostile policy" towards North Korea.
**Pakistan** summoned the US Charge d'Affaires over US Ambassador to India's remarks on Kashmir.
**NATO** officials stated the alliance is prepared to respond to any threats from Iran, citing the interception of Iranian ballistic missiles heading towards Turkey earlier this year.
**Gulf states** are reacting to the regional instability; the UAE has ceased all trade with Iran.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are notable contradictions regarding control and access in the Strait of Hormuz. While President Trump claims the US has "complete control" and facilitates significant oil traffic, a source close to the Iranian negotiation team denies direct US-Iran talks and implies continued Iranian influence by reporting the diversion of an Emirati tanker. The Iranian military's ability to "divert" a tanker in the "northern corridor" contradicts the US claim of having degraded Iranian radar capabilities.

The Syrian Foreign Minister's denial of Turkish military presence at Abu al-Duhur airbase conflicts with Israeli claims that their strike targeted an intended Turkish deployment. This discrepancy could indicate misinformation from either side, a failure of intelligence assessment, or a deliberate diplomatic maneuver. The revelation of a phone call between Mossad Chief Roman Gofman and Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani days prior to the Israeli strike suggests a direct communication channel, but the content of the discussion and any agreements reached remain unverified.

Casualty figures from the Gaza strikes vary between IDF reports (specific Hamas commanders and other operatives targeted) and Palestinian media (overall fatalities and wounded at the police station). This is common in conflict reporting and likely reflects different reporting objectives (IDF on targeting, Palestinian media on overall impact).

The US claim of establishing a "secret" shipping corridor, though reported by Axios, implies a level of operational secrecy that might be compromised by its public announcement, potentially inviting Iranian countermeasures. Iran's claim about targeting 8 Saudi oil tankers and preventing 48 others from crossing are significant and need independent verification to assess their full impact and accuracy.

Overall, the information presents a picture of escalating tensions with potential for rapid, unpredictable developments, particularly concerning the US-Iran relationship, maritime security in the Gulf, and the Israel-Turkey-Syria dynamic.
